messages:
Maria: Heads up — we just saw a sharp latency burst on a few dedicated nodes during our long-context stress tests. Spike correlates with sustained concurrency and many cache reinserts. Looks like eviction churn. Attached pprof and a tiny log excerpt. :eyes:

Jake: Can you paste the log snippet? I want to see eviction/insert counts. Also which policy were those nodes using (LRU or FIFO)?

Maria: Using default LRU on that pool. Log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-18T14:12:01Z INFO kv_cache: evict batch size=128 keys=124 reused=3
2026-03-18T14:12:01Z WARN kv_cache: resident=62.1GB pressure=0.92 page_faults=480
2026-03-18T14:12:02Z INFO kv_cache: insert tok=conv-93827 seq=1024 size=1.2MB
2026-03-18T14:12:02Z INFO rpc: request_latp90=230ms latp99=780ms
```

Sophia: Reproducer steps I used (local with smaller mem):
```
# run long-context concurrency load
./run_infer --model rwd-7b --seq 32k --concurrency 40 --pattern reinserts
```
Pattern reinserts = many short prefixes then long tail that reuses earlier KV entries frequently.

Tony: Hmm. LRU + reinserts can cause thrash if insert rate beats reuse locality. Did you see a lot of page-in syscalls in the profile?

Jake: Yep — pprof shows repeated syscall.OpenFile/pagein spikes and hot stack at `kv::reinsert_node` and `memmgr::evict_candidate_search`. Also noticed mutex contention around the eviction list head.

Maria: Experimented with FIFO on a spare pool for 30m and latency tail dropped: p99 went from ~780ms -> ~210ms under same load. But I'm not 100% sure FIFO correctness for reuse patterns.

Sophia: Interesting. FIFO reduces churn because recently evicted items don't get immediately reinserted to the tail like in LRU? (I know FIFO will evict in insertion order so reinserts might survive longer in some patterns).

Jake: Right. LRU tries to keep recently accessed items; with constant reinserts of large KV blobs, LRU costs O(1) but the memory walking and list updates cause cacheline bouncing. FIFO avoids pointer juggling on hits.

Tony: We should be careful — I remember a subtle correctness issue we had where FIFO reinserts + async reordering produced stale pointer reads in a race. Anyone recall bug id?

Maria: I think that was #INF-412. It was about reinsert ordering not updating generation counters, leading to occasional stale KV returned for a different sequence when paging kicked in. We patched it but maybe the FIFO variant here exposes a different path.

Jake: I ran a focused correctness test: 5000 concurrent short/long mixed sequences with aggressive paging. FIFO returned a stale KV 2/100k requests (reproducible). LRU with the latest patch returned 0. So FIFO fix needed.

Sophia: Can you share the failing trace?

Jake: Trace snippet: 
```
# simplified
reader A loads key K (gen 17)
concurrent evict removes K, writes tombstone
writer B reinserts K -> gen 18 at tail
reader A resumes, sees pointer to old slab (not tombstone) -> serves stale data
```
Cause: reader resumed after partial eviction and resumed before generation check.

Tony: That matches. Solution options: add per-slot generation checks on reads, or make reinsert atomic with tombstone sweep, or add a short grace window where reinserts are pinned until eviction completes. Each has perf tradeoffs.

Maria: I put up an A/B run: group A LRU with lock-free gen-check, group B FIFO with gen-check + extra CAS on reinsert. Early numbers: A p99=210ms, B p99=230ms, correctness failures: A=0, B=0 (after gen-check). CPU overhead for gen-check ~3-5%.

Jake: Gen-check approach looks promising — cheap read path check and prevents stale reads. But it increases per-read memory reads (an extra small load). For tight latency SLOs could be acceptable if p99 stays under target.

Sophia: Also observed KV fragmentation growth over long contexts under LRU: lots of small slabs because reinserts use different allocation sizes. We should consider normalizing slab sizes on reinserts to improve reuse and reduce fragmentation.

Tony: Agreed. Action items I propose: 
- short-term: enable gen-check on reads + enable FIFO as optional policy behind flag for further testing
- medium: implement slab-size normalization on reinserts + hysteresis watermarks to avoid repeated paging loops
- long-term: add deployment-side telemetry to correlate eviction rate, mutex contention, and p99 across pools (per-model/per-sequence-length)

Maria: I'll open a PR with the gen-check patch and a feature flag to flip FIFO. Will include benchmarks and a canary plan.

Jake: Also add a small repro harness that toggles reinserts pattern; saves flamegraph and pages in /tmp so SRE can run it in prod-like infra.

Sophia: If you need quick config to flip FIFO on a pool:
```
# toggle in runtime-config
kv_policy: FIFO
kv_gen_check: true
kv_hysteresis: 0.08
```

Maria: Thanks — putting the canary up now. Will update once we have 2h of stable numbers. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for pool `dedicated-03` with config `kv_policy=FIFO,kv_gen_check=true` at 2026-03-18T16:05:00Z

Maria: Quick update 30m in — p99 improvement holds, no correctness regressions in 1M requests. Some CPU overhead but within budget. Continuing observation window.

Jake: Nice. Once canary completes we should roll to other pools with a staggered schedule + metric alerts for page_faults spike and evict_rate.

Tony: I'll draft a short runbook for on-call: include steps to force FIFO on a pool, check gen-check toggle, and rollback. Keep eviction-watermarks and hysteresis knobs documented.

Maria: Great. Closing loop after 4h canary. Thanks all for quick responses.
